- Model consistently underestimates prices, especially in early periods of the 30-day forecast.
- Forecasts tend to be too low in the first 5–10 days, then gradually rise — suggesting a lag in capturing near-term price momentum.
- After sharp price spikes in history, model forecasts overshoot and then overcorrect, leading to overestimation in the following days.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias — it often predicts a return to historical averages too quickly, missing sustained trends.
- Forecasts for the last 5–7 days of the 30-day window are often too high, possibly due to overconfidence in short-term volatility or failure to account for regulatory or supply-side shocks.
- Model underestimates price volatility in the final 10 days — especially when true outcomes show sudden spikes or corrections.
- Forecasts are overly conservative in the early part of the forecast horizon, failing to capture the “rebound” phase after a dip.
- Model tends to ignore the influence of recent high prices — it underweights recent history when forecasting future values, leading to persistent underestimation.
